ORDER This is the first criminal appeal filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 14-A of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 for grant of anticipatory bail against order dated 02.11.2023 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST, Sagar (M.P.), by which his application for grant of anticipatory bail has been dismissed.

sentences.text:
2 . Appellant is apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR No.371/2023, registered at Police Station Sohagi, District Rewa (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 294, 323, 376 and 506 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(2)(5) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Dharampal Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122298416/
1 (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
3 .
Learned counsel appearing for appellant submitted that as per prosecution version, appellant has forcefully committed rape by throwing her on the ground.
It is submitted that in pre-MLC, no injury has been found on the body of prosecutrix.
Appellant has falsely been implicated in the case due to enmity with Ex-Sarpanch of the village.
Prosecutrix is labourer of said Ex- Sarpanch.
In these circumstances, the appellant may be released on anticipatory bail.
4. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for State opposed the appeal for grant of anticipatory bail.
It is submitted that there is bar under Section 18 of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to grant anticipatory bail to the appellant.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Defence of appellant and other document cannot be considered at this stage.
It is further submitted that as per statement of prosecutrix recorded in Court under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., offence under Section 376 of IPC is made out against the appellant.

Commission of offence under I.P.C. which is punishable with more than 10 years will attract offence under Section 3(2)(5) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Since Act is attracted in the case, bar will become operative and appellant is not entitle to grant anticipatory bail in the case.

Government Advocate appearing for State also submitted that appellant is having two other criminal antecedents and he is a habitual offender.
5. Heard the counsel for the parties.
6. Prosecutrix in her statement has stated that appellant had committed rape on her while she went to agriculture field to answer the call of nature.
Incident was narrated to husband and thereafter report was lodged.

Said allegations made against the appellant makes out offence under Section 3(2)(5) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, therefore,
bar mentioned under Section 18 of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 becomes operative.
7.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In view of bar under Section 18 of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, criminal appeal filed by appellant cannot be entertained and same is dismissed.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE sp/-
